head: af629cf86

boundaries: the production bundle a player downloads
the deploy build on the developer machine

notes: Dependabot #96. One pass, no finding. Performance was not measured: the Browser pane was hidden, which throttles rendering, so all frame-rate readings were discarded rather than recorded. main's own checkout holds LFS pointers for the 3D assets (the LFS server lacks some objects), so real renders used copies from the OmniRave worktree.

instruments.evidence: Dependabot #96 landed as af629cf86: @babylonjs/core and loaders 8.56 -> 9.26, typescript 5.9 -> 7.0, vite 7.3 -> 8.3, vitest 3.2 -> 5.0, jsdom 27 -> 30, @types/node 24 -> 26, plus vite.config.ts and two test files. Boundaries: the production bundle a player downloads, the dev server, the deploy build.
Read 9cc07e6b7 (last review) and the Dependabot memory; #96 had been kept open deliberately, and the user chose to land it knowing the +14% JavaScript.
Printed the build output for both versions: 94 vs 234 JS files, 832 vs 946 KB gzipped in total, the largest chunk 1.54 MB vs 0.75 MB.
The game's markup (HUD, panels) rendered in both versions, dev and production.

instruments.why: No HTTP handler changed; the served files were read as B1 and B5 describe.

instruments.evidence: The config helper and the test helper are the only new names; both are local.
Nothing consumes the upgrade except the game itself.
No duplicated rule.

The consumers of the build: the deploy script builds the game on the developer's Mac (scripts/deploy-lib.sh build_omnirave_locally, Node 23.6, where the build passes) and the server only backs the folder up; dev-omnirave-start.sh runs `npx vite --port 4173`, a flag Vite 8 keeps. No CI workflow builds or tests omnirave-babylon at all, so the local runs are its only check.

The two changed tests now construct their mocks the way the runtime constructs the real classes (with new), and the adaptive test's clock follows the controller's real reading points (frames 30 and 60).
The whole game suite: 1150 tests on both versions.
The adaptive test still fails if the runtime never scales (checked by disabling the scale); it passes on Vitest 3 and 5.
The frontend already runs Vitest 4, which has the same constructor rule; nothing there changes.

instruments.why: No branch changed in game code.
No condition changed in game code.

instruments.evidence: constructible() is one helper per test file, each used by that file only.
Searched every omnirave-babylon test for arrow-function mocks called with new: the 12 in these two files were all of them; the suite passes in full.
tsc --noEmit (TypeScript 7.0.2) 0 errors in the checkout after npm ci; the production build passes; the pre-commit hook passed.

Ran for real, with the real Main Stage and avatar assets copied from the OmniRave worktree (the venue model's SHA-256 matches main's LFS pointer; the avatar bodies are the newer OmniRave version, used on both sides). Dev server, Babylon 8 and 9 side by side: the same view, and per-mesh state identical across all 1195 meshes (64 bucket hashes equal), 505 materials, 23 lights, 1266 textures, the 14 avatar meshes enabled and visible, no console errors. Production build of Babylon 9 served with vite preview: boots on WebGPU (console: Babylon.js v9.26.2), the same scene counts, the avatar visible -- the build a player gets works, including Vite 8's bundling of Babylon's side-effect imports. NOT verified: performance. The Browser pane was hidden, which throttles rendering, so every FPS figure taken (including an apparent 6 FPS, and an apparent hang of Babylon 8's production build) is void and is not reported as a result.
The shape found: a mocked process-wide clock read by the test runner's own loader. Only the one test used a 'once' clock.
1150 of 1150 game tests on both versions with the real assets; without them, the same 2 LFS-dependent files fail on main and on the upgrade alike.
The user's choice: land #96 with its three fixes, accepting about 14% more JavaScript. Dependabot closes #96 once main carries these versions.
The whole game suite, not a selection.
No control patches any file this change touched.
The render check ran the real runtime and the real assets, not a stand-in scene.

gates.tests: omnirave-babylon 1150/1150 with real assets, both versions
